subject: MedVisor Q4 pilot — volume-slab pricing exception request
messages:
From: Sasha Bell <sasha@medvisor.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing for Q4

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. MedVisor is excited to move forward with a 3-month Q4 pilot focused on two models (chat + embeddings) across our triage and clinical search workflows. We expect peak monthly token usage in month 2 to be ~1.2B tokens with steady state ~450M.

Budget note from procurement: they can commit to a minimum spend of $60k over the pilot but are requesting a rate floor that maps to ~40% off published hosted list for the first three months to make the ROI case to clinicians. They specifically want a volume-slab approach (tiered, with aggressive pricing only after a usage threshold).

Can Redwood support a pilot structure like this? If so, what approvals do you need? We tried to model an internal MAE threshold but would prefer to move quickly.

Sasha Bell
Head of Commercial Operations
MedVisor

Looping you both in — MedVisor wants an aggressive pilot pricing structure (40% off list, tiered). They can only commit $60k minimum for pilot. Volume profile attached by Sasha suggests a big spike month 2.

Priyom — can you run quick unit economics on a 3-month pilot at 40% off with the caching/batching profile we discussed? Also include potential Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (they prefer hosted but will consider dedicated capacity if it meaningfully cuts unit cost).

Marissa — this will likely need CFO signoff for a carveout; Marcus I copied so he has context. I'm drafting an exception memo to route for approval. Short on time — suggest we target a final internal decision by EOD 2027-09-14.

Solutions Sales
Redwood Inference

Quoted original message below.
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing for Q4 — MedVisor asks for volume-slab/40% off

Alex / Marissa —

Quick analysis attached (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx) and summary below:

- Assumptions: month1 tokens 450M, month2 peak 1.2B, month3 600M. Model split: 70% chat, 30% embeddings.
- At published hosted list, expected cost to Redwood for pilot (inference + infra) ~ $78k.
- At 40% off list, Redwood revenue for pilot would be ~ $46.8k (below our infra+ops cost as modeled) — negative margin.
- If we apply a volume-slab structure that gives 40% off only on incremental tokens > 750M in month 2, the overall revenue increases to ~$58k (still thin).
- Option: Offer an intro blended concession: 25% off list for first month, then slab with 35% off incremental usage above 750M in month 2. Also require an explicit committed minimum spend of $85k over 3 months to unlock larger discounts.

Recommendation: Provide a conditional exception: allow a maximum of 35% effective discount with a minimum commitment of $85k and an automatic reversion to standard rates if usage or data patterns differ. If the customer wants deeper concession (40% across the board) we need CFO signoff and a structured make-good clause.

I'll attach the unit econ calc and sensitivity table.
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Internal exception memo: MedVisor pilot — request for CFO sign-off

Marcus —

Please find the attached exception memo (medvisor_exception_memo.pdf) and the pricing workbook. TL;DR: MedVisor is asking for an effective 40% discount for a 3-month hosted pilot; risk to Redwood unit economics at that level is material given their projected month-2 spike. Priyom's analysis proposes a compromise structure (blended/volume-slab) with an $85k minimum to protect us.

Key ask: CFO approval to offer a maximum effective 35% concession with contractual guardrails: minimum committed spend $85k, slabed discounts that only apply after threshold, a 30-day make-good clause if usage patterns don't align with projections, and a short-term revenue share clause if usage doubles.

Why approve: MedVisor is a credible strategic healthcare customer (HIT integration, potential enterprise expansion). Approving a limited special pilot could unlock a larger annual deal in H1 2028.

Risks: short-term margin loss, precedent for other medtech pilots, increased SRE support during peak.

I can jump on a call to walk through the numbers; target for a decision by EOD 2027-09-14 to keep procurement timelines moving.

Best,
Alex Martinez
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal exception memo: MedVisor pilot — request for CFO sign-off

Alex / team —

Reviewed Priyom's workbook and your memo. I will approve a constrained exception under the following conditions:

1) Offer the blended concession: 25% off month 1, then slabed discounts with a 35% cap on incremental tokens above 750M in month 2 only. No blanket 40% across the board.
2) Contract must include a firm minimum committed spend of $85k over the 3-month pilot; revenue must be invoiced up front for month 1 and a portion (50%) escrowed for month 2 to cover peak costs.
3) Add an SLO escalation clause: MedVisor must notify us 72 hours in advance of expected >1B token days and purchase burst capacity or shift to Dedicated if sustained.
4) Approval is valid only for this account and must be documented as a one-off executive exception in financial controls. Sales must submit a short post-mortem if costs deviate >20% from the model.

Assuming legal prepares a quick amendment with these guardrails, Alex you have my signoff to proceed.

Marcus
CFO, Redwood Inference
